newsitem.title: USA: Cook County, Ill. head proposes $2.2 bln budget.
newsitem.headline: Cook County, Ill. head proposes $2.2 bln budget.

text.p: Cook County, Ill., Board President John Stroger proposed a $2.2 billion fiscal 1997 budget Thursday that he said lays the groundwork for eliminating a budget defict.
Stroger said that the proposed spending plan "begins to attack the looming structural deficit" that financial advisers last year said could reach $850 million by 2000.
He added the current county budget reduced that deficit projection by more than $300 million.
"The budget I'm presenting today marks my commitment to finding other revenue streams to help support the cost of running county government," Stroger said in his budget message.

To that end, he proposed a package of "alternative revenue streams" to raise $38 million to $40 million for the fiscal 1997 budget. Those were an eight cent hike to 18 cents on the county tax on cigarettes, subject diesel fuel users to the the same charges as gasoline users, and institute a three percent ticket tax for concerts and other events.

Thomas Glaser, the county's chief financial officer, said the budget does not include any new debt issuance. However, he said the county is currently eyeing the possibility of refunding $250 million of outstanding general obligation debt and may consider a debt issue to finance the aquisition of a downtown Chicago building to house county offices.

Glaser added that further debt sales for a new county hospital will not take place until 1998. He pointed out a $487 million bond new and refunding issue the county sold in July provided $114 million in proceeds to get the hospital project started.
The proposed budget is scheduled to come up for a final vote by the Cook County Board on Nov. 22, according to Stroger spokeswoman Andrea Brands. The county's fiscal year begins Dec. 1.
